page: OVHcloud c2-7 is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel processor based on the Haswell architecture without TSX, operating at a dedicated clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs. It is equipped with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.5 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate that the c2-7 instance sits in the lower performance tiers for intensive workloads. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Memory bandwidth tests also show weak to poor performance, with large-block read-only operations recording 20.03 GB/sec. However, the instance achieves an average rating in text generation speed for small language models with 135M parameters, reaching 74.86 tokens/sec, while its prompt processing speed remains weak at 212.61 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2-7 offers dedicated CPU allocation on older Intel hardware, making it a predictable but low-throughput option for non-demanding tasks. The lack of hyperthreading and modern instruction sets like AVX-512 limits its utility for modern vector math or heavy parallel processing. This instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale Redis caching, or simple utility scripts that require dedicated CPU cores but do not demand high memory bandwidth or high-speed network throughput.
